articles/api-authentication.html.title: API Authentication | Organizor
articles/api-authentication.html.summary: API Authentication Overview This document explains how the Organizor API authenticates requests using Keycloak-issued JWT tokens. JWT Validation The API validates tokens using the Keycloak realm: Authority: https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Audience validation: disabled for the current development setup Token type: Bearer The authentication middleware: validates the token signature; validates the issuer; validates token expiration; populates HttpContext.User. Audience validation is intentionally disabled in code while the Keycloak client and token shape are still being finalized. Once the API has a stable audience claim, enable audience validation and document the expected value here. Authentication Flow Frontend logs in via Keycloak. Keycloak issues a JWT. Frontend sends Authorization: Bearer <token>. Frontend also sends X-Tenant-Slug: acme for tenant-scoped routes. API validates the JWT. [Authorize] attributes enforce authentication where applied. Service Accounts The organizor-api client can use the client_credentials flow for internal API-to-API communication. Service account tokens are identified by the client_id claim: "client_id": "organizor-api" Service accounts bypass tenant access checks. WhoAmI Endpoint Example response: { "user": "admin@acme.dev", "tenant": null, "tenantClaims": [ "/tenants/acme/admins" ], "roles": [ "tenant-admin", "tenant-user" ], "claims": [ { "type": "sub", "value": "..." }, { "type": "tenant", "value": "/tenants/acme/admins" }, { "type": "role", "value": "tenant-admin" } ] } Error Codes 401 Unauthorized -> Missing or invalid token. 403 Forbidden -> Token is valid, but the user is not allowed. 400 Bad Request -> Missing or invalid tenant header on tenant-scoped routes. Test Request GET https://localhost:7184/api/auth/whoami Authorization: Bearer <token>

articles/api-integration.html.title: API Integration — High‑Level | Organizor
articles/api-integration.html.summary: API Integration — High‑Level The Portal UI communicates with the Organizor API to perform all business operations. Every action — from loading data to updating records — goes through the API. How Communication Works The Portal uses HttpClient to send requests. A secure access token is automatically added to each request. The API validates the token before processing the request. Local development configuration: Setting Value Portal origin https://localhost:7025 API base URL https://localhost:7184 Authorized URL https://localhost:7184 Token issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev What Developers Should Know API calls are centralized through a configured HttpClient. Authentication is handled automatically. Errors from the API surface in the UI through standard Blazor patterns. If the API authority and portal token issuer differ by scheme, host, or port, API requests will fail with 401 Unauthorized. Why This Matters This approach ensures: Consistent security across the platform A clean separation between UI and backend logic The ability to scale or replace parts of the system independently

articles/api.html.title: Public API Behavior | Organizor
articles/api.html.summary: Public API Behavior The public API currently exposes tenant catalog endpoints. These endpoints are platform/catalog routes, so tenant resolution does not require X-Tenant-Slug for them. They are still authenticated: POST /api/v1/tenants requires organizor-admin. GET /api/v1/tenants and GET /api/v1/tenants/{slug} require organizor-admin, tenant-admin, or tenant-user. Tenant-scoped application endpoints should include the X-Tenant-Slug header unless the path is explicitly skipped by tenant resolution. Internal tenant administration endpoints are documented separately in Internal Operations. Tenant Catalog Create Tenant POST /api/v1/tenants Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme" } Creates a catalog tenant record with Pending status and returns tenant metadata. This route does not provision Keycloak groups, a default tenant admin, or a tenant database. Use POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard for the full onboarding workflow. Example response: { "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "databaseName": "organizor_tenant_acme", "createdAt": "2026-05-15T10:00:00Z" } Possible responses: Status Meaning 200 OK Tenant catalog record was created. 401 Unauthorized Missing or invalid bearer token. 403 Forbidden Token does not satisfy the organizor-admin role policy. 409 Conflict Duplicate tenant slug. 500 Internal Server Error Unexpected server error. See Errors and Observability. Get Tenant By Slug GET /api/v1/tenants/acme Authorization: Bearer <token> Returns a tenant by slug, or 404 Not Found when no tenant exists. Soft-deleted tenants are excluded. List Tenants GET /api/v1/tenants Authorization: Bearer <token> Returns all catalog tenants visible through the tenant repository. Soft-deleted tenants are excluded. Platform Endpoints Endpoint Purpose /health Public health check endpoint. /openapi/v1.json OpenAPI document in development. /scalar Interactive OpenAPI/Scalar endpoint explorer in development. OpenAPI And Scalar When the API runs in development: OpenAPI JSON is available at /openapi/v1.json. Scalar is available at /scalar. Use this article for behavior: routes, authorization expectations, tenant headers, response shapes, and operational meaning. Use the generated API reference only for C# type signatures.

articles/architecture.html.title: Architecture | Organizor
articles/architecture.html.summary: Architecture Organizor follows a layered structure around tenant management. flowchart LR Client[HTTP client] --> Api[Code7Dev.Organizor.Api] Api --> Application[Code7Dev.Organizor.Application] Application --> Domain[Code7Dev.Organizor.Domain] Application --> Infrastructure[Code7Dev.Organizor.Infrastructure] Api --> Quartz[Quartz scheduler] Quartz --> Infrastructure Infrastructure --> Catalog[(Catalog database)] Infrastructure --> TenantDb[(Tenant databases)] API Layer The API project owns transport concerns: controller routes for public tenant catalog operations and internal tenant operations; request and response DTOs; mapping between API DTOs and application models; correlation ID, exception handling, and tenant resolution middleware; Serilog request logging; CORS, health checks, OpenAPI, and Scalar setup. The startup flow in Program.cs composes the application by registering catalog persistence, tenant persistence, application services, infrastructure services, and API services. Application Layer The application project owns use cases and contracts. It defines interfaces for repository access, tenant database management, migration, provisioning, onboarding, upgrades, and lifecycle operations. Current services: Service Responsibility TenantService Creates catalog tenant records and reads tenants by slug or as a list. TenantOnboardingService Creates a catalog tenant, runs provisioning, and marks the tenant active or failed. TenantLifecycleService Soft-deletes tenants and hard-deletes already soft-deleted tenants. TenantUpgradeService Runs migrations for an existing tenant database. Domain Layer The domain project currently contains the tenant entity and status enum. A tenant stores identity, slug, database name, creation date, lifecycle status, provisioning failure reason, and deletion metadata. Infrastructure Layer The infrastructure project owns external resources: CatalogDbContext stores tenant records. OrganizorDbContext connects to the current tenant database after tenant resolution. TenantRepository implements catalog tenant persistence. ConnectionStringBuilder builds PostgreSQL connection strings from configuration. TenantDatabaseManager creates and drops tenant databases. TenantMigrator applies EF Core migrations to tenant databases. TenantProvisioningWorkflow creates a tenant database and applies migrations during onboarding. TenantJobScheduler schedules tenant-scoped Quartz jobs from catalog tenant records. TenantAwareJobFactory creates Quartz jobs through dependency injection. SyncTenantJob runs recurring tenant synchronization work with ITenantContext populated from Quartz job data. Background Jobs Quartz is registered by the API layer and backed by persistent PostgreSQL storage in the catalog database. On startup, the application schedules a recurring synchronization job for each catalog tenant. Each job carries the tenant ID and slug in Quartz job data, then sets the tenant context before running tenant database work. Request Pipeline sequenceDiagram participant Client participant Api participant TenantResolution participant Application participant Infrastructure Client->>Api: HTTP request Api->>Api: Correlation ID and exception handling Api->>TenantResolution: Resolve tenant when required TenantResolution->>Infrastructure: Load tenant by X-Tenant-Slug Infrastructure-->>TenantResolution: Tenant record TenantResolution->>Application: Continue with current tenant context Application->>Infrastructure: Use catalog or tenant database services Infrastructure-->>Application: Result Application-->>Api: Model Api-->>Client: HTTP response

articles/authentication-flow.html.title: Authentication Flow — High‑Level | Organizor
articles/authentication-flow.html.summary: Authentication Flow — High‑Level The Portal UI uses Keycloak to authenticate users and determine what they are allowed to do. The process follows the standard OpenID Connect Authorization Code Flow with PKCE. What Happens During Login The user clicks Login. The Portal redirects the user to Keycloak at https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. Keycloak handles the login form and verifies credentials. After successful login, Keycloak sends the user back to https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback. The Portal receives a secure token and uses it for API requests. Why Keycloak Centralized user management Role‑based access control Secure token handling Standard OIDC protocol support What Developers Need to Know The Portal never handles passwords directly. Tokens are automatically attached to API requests. Protected pages require the user to be authenticated. Keycloak configuration determines what each user can access. The organizor-ui Keycloak client must allow https://localhost:7025/* as a redirect URI and https://localhost:7025 as a web origin.

articles/configuration.html.title: Configuration | Organizor
articles/configuration.html.summary: Configuration Organizor reads standard ASP.NET Core configuration from appsettings.json, environment-specific files, user secrets, and environment variables. Catalog Connection String CatalogDbContext expects a connection string named Catalog. Example shape: { "ConnectionStrings": { "Catalog": "Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=organizor_catalog;Username=postgres;Password=postgres" } } Tenant PostgreSQL Settings ConnectionStringBuilder builds tenant and admin connection strings from the Postgres section. { "Postgres": { "Host": "localhost", "Port": "5432", "User": "postgres", "Password": "postgres" } } The admin connection uses the postgres database. Tenant connections use the tenant database name stored in the catalog. Keycloak The API requires Keycloak settings for two separate concerns: JWT validation uses Keycloak:Authority. Tenant onboarding uses the Keycloak admin client settings to create tenant groups, assign roles, and create the default tenant admin user. Example development shape: { "Keycloak": { "Authority": "https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev", "BaseUrl": "https://localhost:8443", "Realm": "organizor-dev", "AdminClientId": "organizor-api", "AdminClientSecret": "<client-secret>" } } Authority must match the token issuer exactly. The local Keycloak container runs at https://localhost:8443, so tokens from the Blazor portal will have issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev. Store client secrets in user secrets, environment variables, or deployment secrets rather than committing them to source. Portal UI The Blazor WebAssembly portal uses Keycloak for OIDC login and calls the API with bearer tokens. Current local development endpoints: Setting Value Portal URL https://localhost:7025 Keycloak authority https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Keycloak client ID organizor-ui Login callback https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback API base URL https://localhost:7184 These values must stay aligned with the organizor-ui client redirect URIs and web origins in Keycloak. Quartz Quartz uses the Catalog connection string for its persistent store. The same catalog database stores tenant records and Quartz scheduler tables. The API registration configures: PostgreSQL-backed Quartz persistence; Newtonsoft JSON serialization for persisted job data; clustering support; hosted service startup for Quartz background processing. Tenant job scheduling is not enabled on application startup yet. TenantJobScheduler is available for future real tenant jobs, but the startup scheduling block is currently commented out until those jobs exist. Logging Serilog is configured in appsettings.json. Current sinks: console; rolling file logs under logs/log-.txt. Log output includes tenant and request correlation properties when available: Id; Slug; DatabaseName; CorrelationId. CORS The API selects a CORS policy by environment: DevCors in development allows any origin, header, and method. ProdCors outside development must be configured with explicit allowed origins before browser clients can call the API. The current production policy has no origins configured. Treat that as a deployment checklist item, not a complete production setting. OpenAPI and Scalar OpenAPI and Scalar endpoints are mapped only in development. This keeps the production surface smaller while retaining local API exploration during development.

articles/database-provisioning.html.title: Database Provisioning | Organizor
articles/database-provisioning.html.summary: Database Provisioning Organizor uses one catalog database and one PostgreSQL database per tenant. Catalog Database CatalogDbContext stores tenant records in the tenants table. Important constraints: Field Constraint Name Required, max length 200. Slug Required, max length 100, unique index. DatabaseName Required, max length 200. IsDeleted Required, defaults to false. DeletionReason Optional, max length 500. On startup, the API checks whether the catalog database exists, creates it when needed, and applies catalog migrations. The full tenant onboarding workflow is documented in Internal Operations. Database provisioning is one part of that workflow; Keycloak tenant access is provisioned before the tenant database is created. Tenant Database Naming Tenant databases use: organizor_tenant_{slug} Example: organizor_tenant_acme Slugs are normalized to lowercase before tenant records are written. PostgreSQL Requirements The configured PostgreSQL user must be able to: connect to the admin postgres database; create tenant databases; drop tenant databases during hard deletion; create extensions in tenant databases. Tenant database creation currently uses: CREATE DATABASE "{databaseName}" OWNER = postgres ENCODING = 'UTF8'; Each tenant database is initialized with: CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "pgcrypto"; CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "citext"; Hard deletion uses: DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "{databaseName}" WITH (FORCE); Migration Flow TenantMigrator builds a tenant-specific connection string, checks pending migrations on OrganizorDbContext, applies them, and returns: Field Meaning Database Tenant database name. Success Whether migrations completed. AppliedMigrations Count of migrations pending before execution. Duration Migration runtime. Error Error message when migration fails. Onboarding and Cleanup During POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard, the database steps are: create the tenant database named organizor_tenant_{slug}; initialize required PostgreSQL extensions; apply pending OrganizorDbContext migrations; return success so the tenant can be marked Active. If the migration result fails or onboarding throws unexpectedly, the catalog tenant is marked Failed. During hard deletion, the tenant must already be soft-deleted. The hard-delete workflow drops the tenant database with DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS ... WITH (FORCE) after Keycloak cleanup and then removes the catalog record.

articles/errors-and-observability.html.title: Errors and Observability | Organizor
articles/errors-and-observability.html.summary: Errors and Observability Correlation IDs Every request passes through CorrelationIdMiddleware. Clients can provide a correlation ID: X-Correlation-ID: request-123 If the header is missing, the API generates a GUID. The final value is returned in the response header: X-Correlation-ID: 2ad71e7a-13cb-4ef8-a4c7-f3a37ad9dc71 The same value is pushed into Serilog context as CorrelationId. Error Shape Unhandled exceptions are returned as RFC 7807-style problem details: { "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/500", "title": "An unexpected error occurred.", "status": 500, "detail": "Exception message", "instance": "/api/v1/tenants", "correlationId": "2ad71e7a-13cb-4ef8-a4c7-f3a37ad9dc71" } The response content type is: application/problem+json Note The current middleware includes exception messages in detail. Treat that as useful during development, but review it before exposing production environments. Tenant Resolution Errors Tenant-scoped requests require: X-Tenant-Slug: acme Missing tenant slug returns 400 Bad Request with a plain text response. Unknown tenant slug returns 404 Not Found with a plain text response. Log Context Serilog output is configured to include: Property Source CorrelationId Request header or generated GUID. Id Resolved tenant ID. Slug Resolved tenant slug. DatabaseName Tenant database selection when available. SourceContext Logger source in file logs.

This page keeps the shorter first-run flow. Prerequisites .NET SDK 10. PostgreSQL available to the API. Keycloak available to the API. The repository includes a development Keycloak compose file. A catalog database connection string named Catalog. PostgreSQL server settings under the Postgres configuration section for tenant database creation and resolution. Install DocFX if the docfx command is not available: dotnet tool install -g docfx Start the development Keycloak instance: docker compose up -d The compose file starts Keycloak at https://localhost:8443. Generate and trust the local certificate first if keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 does not exist. Configure the organizor-dev realm, clients, roles, and users as described in Keycloak Setup. Run the API From the repository root: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api\Code7Dev.Organizor.Api.csproj Development launch profiles expose: Profile URL http http://localhost:5100 https https://localhost:7184 and http://localhost:5100 On startup the API: configures Serilog; registers catalog and tenant database services; registers application and infrastructure services; seeds or migrates the catalog database; maps controllers, health checks, OpenAPI, and Scalar in development. Development Endpoints Endpoint Purpose /health ASP.NET Core health checks. /openapi/v1.json OpenAPI document, available in development. /scalar Interactive OpenAPI/Scalar endpoint explorer, available in development. Example tenant catalog request: $token = "<organizor-admin JWT>" Invoke-RestMethod ` -Method Post ` -Uri "http://localhost:5100/api/v1/tenants" ` -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } ` -ContentType "application/json" ` -Body '{"name":"Acme","slug":"acme"}' POST /api/v1/tenants creates a catalog record only and requires an organizor-admin token. Use POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard when you also need tenant database and Keycloak provisioning. Run the Portal UI From the repository root: dotnet run --project .\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui\Code7Dev.Organizor.Portal.Ui.csproj --launch-profile https The HTTPS profile exposes the portal at https://localhost:7025. The portal is configured to: authenticate against https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev; use the organizor-ui Keycloak client; receive login callbacks at https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback; call the API at https://localhost:7184. Build the Documentation From the repository root: docfx .\docs\docfx.json DocFX writes the generated site to docs/_site and generated C# type-reference metadata to docs/api. Both folders are ignored by git and can be rebuilt.

articles/internal-operations.html.title: Internal Operations | Organizor
articles/internal-operations.html.summary: Internal Operations This page documents internal routes and workflows for developers and operators. Onboard Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme" } The onboarding flow: normalizes the slug to lowercase; creates a catalog tenant with Pending status; provisions Keycloak tenant groups under /tenants/{slug}; assigns tenant-admin to /tenants/{slug}/admins and tenant-user to /tenants/{slug}/users; creates a default tenant admin user named {slug}-admin with a temporary password of ChangeMe123!; creates the tenant database using organizor_tenant_{slug}; initializes PostgreSQL extensions; applies tenant migrations; marks the tenant Active on success or Failed on provisioning failure. Example response: { "id": "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111", "name": "Acme", "slug": "acme", "databaseName": "organizor_tenant_acme" } Upgrade Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/upgrade Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Runs pending migrations for the tenant database. Example response: { "database": "organizor_tenant_acme", "success": true, "appliedMigrations": 2, "duration": "00:00:01.2340000", "error": null } Soft Delete Tenant DELETE /api/admin/tenants/{id} Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Content-Type: application/json { "reason": "Customer cancellation" } Soft deletion marks the tenant as deleted, stores deletion metadata, and sets status to Deleted. The tenant database is not dropped. Hard Delete Tenant POST /api/admin/tenants/{id}/hard-delete Authorization: Bearer <organizor-admin-token> Hard deletion requires the tenant to already be soft-deleted. It: deletes the default Keycloak admin user named {slug}-admin when it exists; deletes the Keycloak tenant group /tenants/{slug} when it exists; drops the tenant database; removes the catalog record. Keycloak cleanup tolerates missing groups or users so a partially-provisioned tenant can still be cleaned up. Scheduled Tenant Jobs Organizor is wired for Quartz recurring background work, but tenant job scheduling is not currently enabled on startup. Program.cs contains a commented-out scheduling block for future use. The scheduler: loads all tenants from the catalog database; creates a durable SyncTenantJob with job key sync-{tenantId} in the tenant-jobs group; stores TenantId and TenantSlug in the Quartz job data map; creates a trigger named sync-{tenantId}-trigger in the tenant-triggers group; schedules the job when it is new, or replaces and reschedules it when it already exists. Current trigger cadence: 0/10 * * * * ? That Quartz cron expression would run the tenant synchronization job every 10 seconds when scheduling is enabled. SyncTenantJob reads the tenant data from the job data map, sets ITenantContext, and then runs tenant-scoped work through OrganizorDbContext. The current implementation logs execution and contains placeholder synchronization work. Quartz persistence is stored in the catalog database and uses the PostgreSQL tables added by the AddQuartzTables migration. The API configures Quartz with the Catalog connection string, JSON serialization, and clustering enabled. Documentation Deployment The repository contains a GitHub Actions workflow at .github/workflows/docfx-deploy.yml. On pushes to master, it: checks out this repository; installs DocFX; builds docs/docfx.json; checks out the public documentation repository; copies docs/_site into that repository; commits and pushes the generated documentation. The workflow uses the DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY secret to push to the public docs repository. articles/introduction.html.title: Introduction | Organizor
articles/introduction.html.summary: Introduction Organizor is the backend API for managing tenant environments. It keeps tenant records in a central catalog database and provisions a separate PostgreSQL database for each tenant. The current implementation focuses on tenant lifecycle operations: creating tenant catalog records; onboarding tenants by creating a tenant database and applying migrations through internal operations; resolving tenant context for tenant-scoped requests; upgrading tenant databases by running migrations; soft-deleting tenants before hard deletion; exposing health checks, OpenAPI JSON, and Scalar endpoint exploration in development. Main Concepts Concept Description Tenant A customer or isolated workspace tracked by Id, Name, Slug, DatabaseName, lifecycle status, and deletion metadata. Catalog database Central PostgreSQL database that stores all tenant records. Tenant database PostgreSQL database named from the tenant slug, currently using the organizor_tenant_{slug} convention. Tenant resolution Middleware step that reads X-Tenant-Slug, loads the tenant, and stores the current tenant in ITenantContext. Provisioning workflow Infrastructure workflow that creates the tenant database and applies tenant migrations. Project Layout Project Responsibility Code7Dev.Organizor.Api ASP.NET Core host, controllers, DTOs, mappers, middleware, OpenAPI/Scalar, health checks, CORS, and logging setup. Code7Dev.Organizor.Application Tenant service contracts, tenant models, onboarding, lifecycle, upgrade, and catalog-facing application logic. Code7Dev.Organizor.Domain Tenant entity and TenantStatus enum. Code7Dev.Organizor.Infrastructure EF Core contexts, repository implementation, PostgreSQL connection string building, database creation/deletion, migration, and tenant context storage. Documentation Boundaries The documentation is split into two intentionally different areas: Area Purpose Conceptual docs Explain behavior, workflows, configuration, security, local development, operations, and integration decisions. Generated API reference Lists C# namespaces, classes, interfaces, methods, and signatures generated from source. Do not use the generated reference to explain workflows or product behavior. Keep that content in the conceptual articles so it stays readable and can include context, examples, and operational guidance.

articles/keycloak-https.html.title: Keycloak HTTPS Setup | Organizor
articles/keycloak-https.html.summary: Keycloak HTTPS Setup The development Keycloak container runs over HTTPS at https://localhost:8443. The Blazor WebAssembly portal uses this endpoint for OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE, and the API uses the same realm issuer when validating bearer tokens. Why HTTPS Is Required The portal runs as a browser application and should not mix HTTPS portal/API calls with HTTP identity-provider redirects. OIDC redirect URIs must match the portal origin exactly. Keycloak 24 runs with explicit hostname and HTTPS configuration when started in production mode. Local HTTPS keeps browser, API, and identity-provider behavior closer to production. Certificate The compose file mounts a PKCS#12 certificate from: keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 Generate a trusted local certificate with mkcert: mkcert -install mkcert -pkcs12 -p12-file .\keycloak\certs\keycloak.p12 localhost mkcert PKCS#12 files use the password changeit, which matches the Docker Compose configuration. Keep generated certificates out of source control. If the certificate is missing or not trusted, Keycloak may fail to start or the browser may reject the login page. Docker Compose The Keycloak service uses production mode with an HTTPS keystore: keycloak: image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:24.0 command: - start - --hostname=localhost - --https-port=8443 - --https-key-store-file=/opt/keycloak/conf/keycloak.p12 - --https-key-store-password=changeit volumes: - ./keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12:/opt/keycloak/conf/keycloak.p12 ports: - "8443:8443" Start or restart Keycloak from the repository root: docker compose down docker compose up -d Open the admin console at: https://localhost:8443 Development admin credentials are configured in docker-compose.yml: admin / admin Browser Trust Chrome and Edge normally trust the mkcert root certificate through the Windows certificate store after mkcert -install. If Edge still reports ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID, import the mkcert root certificate manually into Trusted Root Certification Authorities: %LOCALAPPDATA%\mkcert\rootCA.pem Then restart the browser. Expected Local Endpoints Component URL Keycloak https://localhost:8443 Keycloak realm issuer https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Portal UI https://localhost:7025 API HTTPS profile https://localhost:7184 The portal and API must both use the HTTPS Keycloak authority. Tokens issued by https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev will not validate against an API configured for the old HTTP Keycloak endpoint. Troubleshooting Symptom Likely cause Fix Keycloak does not start Missing keycloak/certs/keycloak.p12 Generate the certificate with mkcert. Browser rejects Keycloak mkcert root CA is not trusted Run mkcert -install or import the root CA manually. Portal login redirects fail Keycloak client redirect URI does not include https://localhost:7025/* Update the organizor-ui client redirect URIs. API returns 401 for portal tokens API Keycloak:Authority still points to HTTP Set authority to https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev.

articles/keycloak-setup.html.summary: Keycloak Setup This document describes the Keycloak configuration for the Organizor development environment. It includes realm setup, API/UI clients, tenant groups, claim mapping, user/role setup, and the admin-client permissions used by tenant onboarding. The local Keycloak container is expected to run over HTTPS at https://localhost:8443. See Keycloak HTTPS Setup before configuring clients. Realm Setup Open Keycloak Admin Console. Realm dropdown -> Create Realm. Name: organizor-dev. Save. API Client (organizor-api) Settings: Client type: OpenID Connect Client ID: organizor-api Name: Organizor API Required values: Client authentication: ON Authorization: OFF Standard flow: OFF Direct access grants: ON Implicit flow: OFF Service accounts roles: ON Credentials: Open the Credentials tab. Copy the Client Secret. Store it in development tooling that requests tokens. The API currently validates bearer tokens only; it does not read the client secret from application configuration. The client secret is only needed by tooling or services that request tokens with the client_credentials flow. The infrastructure Keycloak admin client also uses this client secret during tenant onboarding. Configure these application settings from the same Keycloak client: { "Keycloak": { "Authority": "https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev", "BaseUrl": "https://localhost:8443", "Realm": "organizor-dev", "AdminClientId": "organizor-api", "AdminClientSecret": "<client-secret>" } } For tenant onboarding and hard deletion, the organizor-api service account must be allowed to use the Keycloak Admin REST API. Assign the required realm-management client roles for: reading groups and users; creating and deleting tenant groups; assigning realm roles to groups; creating the default tenant admin user; resetting the default tenant admin password; adding users to groups; deleting the default tenant admin user during hard deletion. UI Client (organizor-ui) Settings: Client type: OpenID Connect Client ID: organizor-ui Name: Organizor UI Required values: Client authentication: OFF Authorization: OFF Standard flow: ON Direct access grants: OFF Implicit flow: OFF Service accounts roles: OFF Development redirect URIs: https://localhost:7025/* https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback http://localhost:5080/* Web origins: https://localhost:7025 http://localhost:5080 Use * only for quick local testing. Explicit origins are preferable because they catch redirect and CORS mistakes earlier. Tenant Groups Tenant onboarding creates the group structure automatically when POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard is used. Manual setup is only needed for bootstrap or testing. Group structure: /tenants /tenants/acme /tenants/acme/users /tenants/acme/admins Each tenant has: /users group /admins group On onboarding, Organizor assigns: tenant-admin to /tenants/{slug}/admins; tenant-user to /tenants/{slug}/users. It also creates a default tenant admin user: Username: {slug}-admin Email: {slug}-admin@organizor.local Temporary password: ChangeMe123! Group: /tenants/{slug}/admins During hard deletion, Organizor removes the tenant group /tenants/{slug} and deletes the default {slug}-admin user when it exists. Tenant Membership Claim Mapper Location: Clients -> organizor-api Client scopes -> organizor-api-dedicated Mappers -> Create Values: Name: tenant-membership Mapper type: Group Membership Token Claim Name: tenant Full group path: ON Add to ID token: ON Add to access token: ON Add to userinfo: ON User Setup Create these realm roles before assigning users: organizor-admin tenant-admin tenant-user Platform admin: Username: admin@organizor.dev Password: Admin123! Assign realm role: organizor-admin No tenant groups assigned Tenant admin: Username: admin@acme.dev Password: Admin123! Assign realm role: tenant-admin Assign group: /tenants/acme/admins Tenant user: Username: user@acme.dev Password: Admin123! Assign realm role: tenant-user Assign group: /tenants/acme/users Token Testing Token endpoint: https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev/protocol/openid-connect/token Expected role claim examples: { "realm_access": { "roles": ["organizor-admin"] }, "resource_access": { "organizor-api": { "roles": ["tenant-user"] } } } Example tenant claim: "tenant": ["/tenants/acme/admins"] Keycloak Architecture Diagram flowchart TD subgraph Realm["organizor-dev Realm"] APIClient["Client: organizor-api"] UIClient["Client: organizor-ui"] Groups["Tenant Groups"] Mapper["Claim Mapper: tenant-membership"] Users["Users + Roles"] end subgraph Backend["Organizor API (.NET)"] Auth["JWT Validation"] TenantAccess["Tenant Access Middleware"] Controllers["Controllers"] end subgraph Frontend["Organizor UI"] Login["OIDC Login Flow"] end UIClient --> Keycloak[(Keycloak Login UI)] Keycloak --> UIClient UIClient --> Backend APIClient --> Keycloak Keycloak --> APIClient Users --> Groups Groups --> Mapper Mapper --> Keycloak Backend --> Auth --> TenantAccess --> Controllers

articles/localization.html.title: Localization | Organizor
articles/localization.html.summary: Localization Organizor provides multilingual support for error responses using a simple, predictable, API-friendly localization pipeline. Supported Languages Organizor currently supports: en - English (fallback) nl - Dutch Additional languages can be added by creating new resource files in the Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources folder. How Localization Works Localization is driven by the standard Accept-Language HTTP header. Example: Accept-Language: nl The API resolves the culture for the request and uses it to translate error messages. If a translation is missing, the system falls back to English (en). Key Principles Application services return error codes only, such as TENANT_NOT_FOUND. The API middleware maps those codes to localized resource strings. No hardcoded user-facing messages exist in the domain or application layers. Localization is deterministic and client-controlled. Culture Resolution Organizor uses the following resolution order: Accept-Language header. Fallback to English (en). This keeps behavior predictable and client-controlled. Error Code Translation Each error code corresponds to a resource key. Examples: TENANT_NOT_FOUND TENANT_ALREADY_EXISTS UNEXPECTED_ERROR These keys exist in: Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources/Shared.en.resx Code7Dev.Organizor.Api/Resources/Shared.nl.resx The middleware retrieves the localized string and injects it into the RFC 7807 problem response. Example Request and Response Request: GET /api/v1/tenants/unknown Authorization: Bearer <token> Accept-Language: nl Response: { "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/404", "title": "Tenant niet gevonden", "status": 404, "error": "TENANT_NOT_FOUND", "correlationId": "abc123" } The error code remains stable and language-independent. The title is localized based on the request culture. Adding New Translations To add a new language: Create a new .resx file, for example Shared.fr.resx. Add the same error keys as in the English file. Provide translated values. Register the culture in AddApiLocalization. Restart the API.

articles/portal-overview.html.title: Portal UI Overview | Organizor
articles/portal-overview.html.summary: Portal UI Overview The Portal UI is the front‑end application of the Organizor platform. It provides the user‑facing interface for authentication, tenant selection, navigation, and all customer‑side functionality. This document gives a high‑level overview of the Portal UI architecture, its responsibilities, and how it integrates with the backend services. Purpose of the Portal UI Provide a clean and intuitive interface for end‑users. Handle authentication and session management via Keycloak. Communicate with the Organizor API using secure access tokens. Render tenant‑specific data and enforce authorization rules. Serve as the entry point for all customer‑facing features. Technology Stack Blazor WebAssembly for client‑side rendering. .NET 10 for the portal runtime and API integration. Keycloak for authentication (OIDC + PKCE). Component‑based architecture for maintainability. High‑Level Structure The Portal UI is organized into: Pages — top‑level routes (e.g., /dashboard, /profile) Components — reusable UI building blocks Services — API clients, auth handlers, state management Layouts — shared UI shells (navigation, headers, footers) wwwroot — static assets Authentication Flow The Portal UI uses: OIDC Authorization Code Flow with PKCE Keycloak as the identity provider Access tokens for API calls Refresh tokens handled by Keycloak session Current local configuration: Setting Value Portal origin https://localhost:7025 Keycloak authority https://localhost:8443/realms/organizor-dev Keycloak client organizor-ui Login callback https://localhost:7025/authentication/login-callback Logout callback https://localhost:7025/ See: Authentication Flow → authentication-flow.md API Integration The Portal UI communicates with the Organizor API using: Typed HttpClient instances AuthorizationMessageHandler Automatic token injection Tenant‑aware endpoints The local portal API client targets https://localhost:7184 and attaches tokens issued by the organizor-dev realm. See: API Integration → api-integration.md Summary The Portal UI is a modular, secure, and scalable front‑end built on Blazor WebAssembly. It integrates tightly with Keycloak for authentication and the Organizor API for data access, providing a seamless experience for end‑users.

articles/role-based-authorization.html.title: Role-Based Authorization | Organizor
articles/role-based-authorization.html.summary: Role-Based Authorization Overview The API authorizes requests with ASP.NET Core policies backed by Keycloak roles. Authentication validates the JWT first, tenant access middleware enforces tenant membership next, and endpoint authorization policies run after that. Roles Role Purpose organizor-admin Platform administrator. Can manage tenants and call admin operations. tenant-admin Tenant administrator. Can use tenant-aware application endpoints and tenant catalog reads. tenant-user Tenant member. Can use shared tenant-aware application endpoints and tenant catalog reads. JWT Role Sources The API maps these Keycloak claim shapes to ASP.NET Core role claims: { "realm_access": { "roles": ["organizor-admin"] }, "resource_access": { "organizor-api": { "roles": ["tenant-user"] } } } Only client roles under resource_access.organizor-api.roles are promoted. Roles for other clients, such as account, are ignored for API authorization. Policies Policy Accepted roles RequireOrganizorAdminRole organizor-admin RequireTenantUserRole organizor-admin, tenant-admin, tenant-user RequireTenantAdminRole organizor-admin, tenant-admin Use policies for new endpoints unless the endpoint is intentionally authentication-only. [Authorize(Policy = AuthorizationPolicies.RequireOrganizorAdminRole)] Current Endpoint Enforcement Endpoint area Policy /api/admin/tenants/* RequireOrganizorAdminRole POST /api/v1/tenants RequireOrganizorAdminRole GET /api/v1/tenants RequireTenantUserRole GET /api/v1/tenants/{slug} RequireTenantUserRole GET /api/auth/whoami authenticated user only Tenant Interaction Role checks do not replace tenant checks. For tenant-scoped routes, a user must pass both: Tenant authorization in TenantAccessMiddleware. Endpoint role or policy authorization in ASP.NET Core. This means a tenant-user token for acme is still denied when it sends X-Tenant-Slug: contoso. Assigning Roles in Keycloak Realm roles are assigned from the user details screen: Open Keycloak Admin Console. Select the organizor-dev realm. Open Users and select the user. Open Role mapping. Assign one of organizor-admin, tenant-admin, or tenant-user. Client roles can also be assigned under the organizor-api client. If client roles are used, verify they appear in resource_access.organizor-api.roles. Test Matrix Scenario Expected organizor-admin calls /api/admin/tenants Allowed tenant-user calls /api/admin/tenants 403 Forbidden tenant-admin calls GET /api/v1/tenants Allowed tenant-user calls GET /api/v1/tenants Allowed Token has no Organizor role and calls protected endpoint 403 Forbidden Valid role with wrong tenant slug on tenant-scoped route 403 Forbidden

articles/security.html.title: Security | Organizor
articles/security.html.summary: Security CORS Development CORS allows any origin, method, and header. Production CORS currently uses ProdCors, but no production origins are configured in code. Add explicit origins before relying on browser clients in production. Internal Admin Routes Routes under /api/admin/tenants are internal operations routes. They perform provisioning, upgrades, soft deletion, and hard deletion. These endpoints require the RequireAdminRole policy. Only tokens with the organizor-admin role can call them. Error Detail Unhandled exceptions currently include ex.Message in problem details. This is useful for internal development and AI-assisted debugging, but it may expose sensitive implementation details in production. Tenant Resolution Tenant-scoped routes depend on X-Tenant-Slug. Platform routes such as /api/v1/tenants, /api/admin, /health, /openapi, and /scalar skip tenant resolution. Destructive Operations Hard deletion drops the tenant database. The service requires a tenant to be soft-deleted before hard deletion, which protects active tenants from immediate physical removal.

articles/tenancy.html.title: Tenancy | Organizor
articles/tenancy.html.summary: Tenancy Organizor uses catalog-driven, database-per-tenant tenancy. Tenant Catalog The catalog database stores tenant metadata through CatalogDbContext. Each tenant includes: Id; Name; Slug; DatabaseName; CreatedAt; Status; FailureReason; soft-delete metadata. The database name convention is organizor_tenant_{slug}. Slugs are normalized to lowercase before they are stored or used for lookups. Normal catalog reads exclude soft-deleted tenants. Repository methods can include soft-deleted records when an internal operation explicitly asks for them. Tenant Statuses Status Meaning Pending Tenant exists in the catalog but provisioning is not complete. Active Tenant provisioning completed successfully. Upgrading Reserved for upgrade lifecycle state. Failed Provisioning failed or an unexpected onboarding error occurred. Deleted Tenant has been soft-deleted. Tenant Resolution TenantResolutionMiddleware resolves tenant context for tenant-scoped routes. It skips platform endpoints such as: /api/admin; /api/v1/tenants; /health; /scalar; /openapi; root and common static paths. For tenant-scoped requests, clients must send: X-Tenant-Slug: acme The middleware loads the tenant from the catalog and stores TenantInfo in ITenantContext. If the header is missing, the response is 400 Bad Request. If the slug does not match a catalog tenant, the response is 404 Not Found. Tenant Database Resolution OrganizorDbContext uses a fallback in-memory database when no tenant has been resolved. This supports startup, Scalar, migrations, and design-time tooling. When a tenant is resolved, PerTenantDbResolver loads the catalog tenant, builds a PostgreSQL connection string for that tenant database, and OrganizorDbContext uses that database. Tenant Onboarding Flow flowchart TD A[Onboard request] --> B[Create catalog tenant as Pending] B --> C[Create Keycloak tenant groups] C --> D[Assign tenant roles to groups] D --> E[Create default tenant admin] E --> F[Create tenant database] F --> G[Apply tenant migrations] G --> H{Success?} H -->|Yes| I[Mark tenant Active] H -->|No| J[Mark tenant Failed] The preferred full tenant creation route is POST /api/admin/tenants/onboard. It creates the catalog record, provisions Keycloak tenant access, creates the tenant database, applies migrations, and marks the tenant Active only after the workflow succeeds. POST /api/v1/tenants creates only the catalog record with Pending status. It does not create Keycloak groups or a tenant database. Hard deletion is intentionally guarded: the tenant must be soft-deleted before TenantLifecycleService runs the hard-delete workflow. That workflow removes the Keycloak tenant group and default admin user, drops the tenant database, and removes the catalog record.

articles/tenant-authorization.html.title: Tenant Authorization | Organizor
articles/tenant-authorization.html.summary: Tenant Authorization Overview Tenant-scoped API routes require both a valid JWT and an X-Tenant-Slug header. The API resolves the header to a catalog tenant, validates that the JWT is allowed to use that tenant, then lets controller authorization policies run. Tenant Resolution Tenant-scoped routes must include: X-Tenant-Slug: acme The tenant resolution middleware skips platform and infrastructure routes, including: /api/admin /api/v1/tenants /api/auth /health /openapi /scalar /favicon /robots Resolution steps: Middleware reads X-Tenant-Slug. Middleware looks up the tenant in the catalog database. Middleware sets tenantContext.Current. Middleware logs tenant metadata. JWT Tenant Claim Tenant membership is represented by one or more tenant claims. The middleware accepts either direct slugs or Keycloak-style paths: { "tenant": ["/tenants/acme/admins", "/tenants/contoso/users"] } The slug is extracted from the segment after /tenants/. For /tenants/acme/admins, the effective tenant slug is acme. Enforcement Rules For tenant-scoped routes: Missing or invalid Authorization returns 401 Unauthorized when the endpoint requires [Authorize]. Missing X-Tenant-Slug returns 400 Bad Request. Unknown X-Tenant-Slug returns 404 Not Found. A JWT with tenant claims must include the same slug as X-Tenant-Slug. A JWT tenant/header mismatch returns 403 Forbidden. A JWT without tenant claims is treated as a platform superadmin token and bypasses tenant membership checks. The organizor-api service account, identified by client_id = organizor-api, bypasses tenant membership checks. Matching tenant JWTs are still checked through ITenantAccessService.UserHasAccessAsync(userId, tenantId). If ITenantAccessService denies access, the API returns 403 Forbidden. Middleware Chain flowchart TD A[Request] --> B[TenantResolutionMiddleware] B --> C[Authentication] C --> D[TenantAccessMiddleware] D --> E[Authorization Policies] E --> F[Controller] HTTP Test Matrix Scenario Authorization X-Tenant-Slug Expected Tenant token for acme calls acme tenant JWT acme Allowed if ITenantAccessService allows Tenant token for acme calls contoso tenant JWT contoso 403 Forbidden Superadmin token has no tenant claim superadmin JWT any valid slug Allowed Service account token client_id = organizor-api any valid slug Allowed Missing tenant header on tenant route valid JWT omitted 400 Bad Request Unknown tenant header on tenant route valid JWT unknown slug 404 Not Found Missing token on authorized route omitted valid slug 401 Unauthorized ITenantAccessService denies matching user tenant JWT matching slug 403 Forbidden Sample Requests Tenant-scoped request: GET http://localhost:5100/api/some-tenant-scoped-route Authorization: Bearer <tenant-token> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Accept: application/json Cross-tenant denial: GET http://localhost:5100/api/some-tenant-scoped-route Authorization: Bearer <token-with-tenant-acme> X-Tenant-Slug: contoso Accept: application/json Superadmin bypass: GET http://localhost:5100/api/some-tenant-scoped-route Authorization: Bearer <token-without-tenant-claim> X-Tenant-Slug: acme Accept: application/json
